title: Coastal state trials solar-powered ferries on river routes
summary: A coastal state has begun a three-month trial of solar-powered ferries on two busy river crossings. Officials say the boats cost far less to run than diesel ones and produce no fumes. Commuters welcomed the quiet ride, though some boatmen worry about their jobs. The transport department will publish a cost report before expanding the pilot.

title: Metro city opens night libraries to ease exam stress
summary: A metro city has opened five public libraries until midnight during the exam season. Students can use quiet study rooms, free Wi-Fi and a small canteen. Organisers say the first week saw packed halls every evening. Parents' groups praised the idea, while some residents asked whether the city should first fix crowded classrooms and unreliable power in school buildings.

title: Mobile health vans reach remote hill villages
summary: Three mobile health vans have started visiting remote hill villages that once had no clinic within a day's travel. Each van carries a doctor, a nurse and basic diagnostic equipment. Residents say routine check-ups no longer mean losing a day's wages. The district office plans to add two more vans if funding is approved in the next budget.

title: State board proposes coding as a Class 8 subject
summary: A state education board has proposed making basic coding a regular subject from Class 8. The draft syllabus covers logic puzzles, simple programs and online safety. Supporters say it prepares students for future jobs. Teachers' unions argue that many schools lack computers and trained staff, and they want a phased rollout. The board will take public feedback for thirty days.

title: Farmers' cooperative launches shared cold storage
summary: A farmers' cooperative has opened a shared cold-storage unit that lets small growers keep fruit and vegetables fresh for up to three weeks. Members pay a small monthly fee based on how much they store. Early users say they sold produce at better prices instead of rushing to market. The cooperative hopes to open two more units next year.

title: Island nations agree on shared tsunami alert system
summary: Leaders of twelve island nations have agreed to build a shared tsunami warning network. Sensors on the seabed will send alerts to every member country within minutes, so small governments do not need separate systems. The cost will be split by population size. Experts welcomed the deal but warned that sirens and evacuation drills in coastal villages will matter just as much.

title: Northern Union passes law limiting single-use packaging
summary: Lawmakers in the Northern Union have passed a law that will ban single-use plastic packaging for most fresh food by 2029. Supermarkets must offer refill stations and paper alternatives. Environmental groups called it a landmark step. Food producers warned that costs may rise and asked for more time, while the government promised grants for smaller businesses.

title: Port workers end week-long strike after new pay deal
summary: Dock workers at a major shipping port have ended a week-long strike after accepting a revised pay agreement. The deal includes a wage rise, safer shift limits and extra rest days. Hundreds of cargo ships had been delayed, and traders hope the backlog will clear within ten days. Union leaders said they would watch closely to see the promises kept.

title: River water summit ends with interim sharing pact
summary: Three neighbouring countries have signed an interim agreement on sharing water from a long river after a four-day summit. The pact sets seasonal limits on how much each side may draw and creates a joint monitoring team. Negotiators said a permanent treaty is still far off. Farmers downstream hope the deal will end the dry-season shortages of recent years.

title: Startup shows phone battery that charges in ten minutes
summary: A young hardware startup has demonstrated a phone battery that reaches a full charge in about ten minutes. The company says the design uses a new electrode material that stays cool while charging. Independent testers have not yet verified the claims or checked how many charge cycles it survives. The firm hopes to ship its first phones with the battery next year.

title: Open-source group releases privacy-first maps toolkit
summary: A volunteer open-source group has released a mapping toolkit that keeps location data on the user's device. App makers can add offline maps and route planning without sending trips to a central server. Developers praised the clear documentation. The group says it relies on donations, and it is asking companies that use the code to help pay for maintenance.

title: Survey: most teens want clear labels on AI-made content
summary: A survey of two thousand teenagers found that most want clear labels on images, videos and text made by artificial intelligence. Many said they had been fooled by fake content at least once. Researchers noted that opinions were split on who should enforce labels, with some favouring platforms and others preferring laws. The study will be repeated next year.

title: Lab demonstrates error-corrected quantum memory chip
summary: Researchers at Brightwell Labs say they have built a small quantum memory chip that corrects its own errors long enough to be useful for experiments. The result is an early step, and the device holds only a handful of quantum bits. Outside scientists called it promising but cautioned that practical quantum computers remain many years away and need much larger systems.

title: Regional carriers begin rolling out satellite messaging
summary: Two regional phone carriers have begun offering satellite messaging for areas with no mobile coverage. Customers can send short texts and emergency alerts from hills, forests and open sea using a normal handset. The service is included in premium plans for now. Consumer groups want it added to basic plans because remote travellers are the people who need it most.

title: Underdog club reaches national cup final
summary: A small-town football club has reached the national cup final after a dramatic penalty shoot-out in the semi-final. The team, made up mostly of part-time players with day jobs, beat two top-division sides on the way. Local shops have closed early to let fans travel to the capital. The final will be played at the national stadium next Saturday.

title: Teen sprinter breaks under-18 record in 100 metres
summary: A seventeen-year-old sprinter has broken the national under-18 record for the 100 metres, finishing in just over ten and a half seconds at a regional meet. Her coach said the result came from steady training rather than any shortcut. She now hopes to be picked for the junior championships. Officials will confirm the record once the timing data is checked.

title: Cricket board trials shorter evening matches for schools
summary: The state cricket board will trial shorter evening matches for school teams, with each side playing twenty overs in under two hours. Organisers say the format lets more children play after classes and keeps parents watching. Some coaches worry that shorter games give young batters less time to learn patience. Results of the trial will be reviewed at the end of the term.

title: Marathon organisers set equal prize money for wheelchair race
summary: Organisers of a popular city marathon have announced that wheelchair racers will receive the same prize money as runners from next year. They also plan a separate starting slot and a smoother course with fewer sharp turns. Athletes called the decision overdue. The race director said sponsors had agreed to cover the extra cost and that registrations open next month.

title: Small-business loan app sees record sign-ups
summary: A digital lending app aimed at shopkeepers and street vendors says it signed up half a million new users in a month. Loans are small and approved within hours using sales records rather than collateral. Banking experts welcomed the access to credit but urged users to check interest rates carefully, as short-term loans can become expensive if repayments are missed.

title: Retail chain to cut plastic from home deliveries
summary: A national retail chain says it will replace plastic bags and bubble wrap in home deliveries with paper and reusable crates by next spring. Customers will be able to return crates on the next order. The company expects a small rise in packing costs but says it will not raise prices. Environmental groups asked for regular public reports on progress.

title: Fuel prices ease for third straight month
summary: Fuel prices have eased for the third month in a row, helped by steady supply and softer global demand. Petrol and diesel are now cheaper than at the start of the year. Transport operators say the relief is modest and has not yet reached food prices. Economists expect rates to stay stable through winter unless supply is disrupted again.

title: Co-working spaces spread to smaller towns
summary: Co-working spaces are opening in smaller towns as more people keep remote jobs after moving closer to family. Operators say demand is highest from software testers, designers and online tutors who need reliable internet. Rents are far lower than in big cities. Local councils see the centres as a way to keep young workers from leaving, and some offer tax breaks.

title: Researchers map a deep-sea coral nursery
summary: Marine scientists using a remote-controlled submersible have mapped a deep-sea coral nursery where young corals attach to the rocks in large numbers. The site lies far below the surface and had never been surveyed. Researchers say it could help restore damaged reefs elsewhere. They are asking the government to protect the area from trawling until further studies are complete.

title: Telescope team spots unusually bright comet
summary: An international telescope team has spotted a comet that is brighter than expected for its distance from the sun. Astronomers say it may become visible to the naked eye in a few months if it keeps brightening. Comets can fade suddenly, so predictions remain uncertain. Amateur observers are being asked to share photos so that its path can be tracked more closely.

title: Soil microbe mix lifts crop yields in drought trial
summary: A three-year field trial found that a mix of natural soil microbes helped wheat and millet fields produce more grain during dry seasons. Researchers say the microbes help roots absorb water and nutrients. Yields rose in most test farms but not in all, and results varied with soil type. A wider trial is planned before the product is offered to farmers.
